summary: ADHD is a neurodevelopmental condition that affects attention, impulse control, and activity levels. It often starts in childhood and frequently continues into adulthood, though symptoms can look different at different ages.
causes: premature birth or low birth weight
prenatal exposure to alcohol or nicotine

summary: PCOS is a hormonal condition affecting people with ovaries, often involving irregular periods, higher levels of male-type hormones, and small cysts on the ovaries. It is a common cause of fertility difficulties and can affect metabolism and weight.
symptoms: weight gain or trouble losing weight
treatments: birth control pills to regulate periods

summary: Lupus is a chronic autoimmune disease where the immune system mistakenly attacks healthy tissue throughout the body. It can affect the skin, joints, kidneys, brain, and other organs, and often comes and goes in flares.
symptoms: butterfly-shaped rash across cheeks and nose
causes: environmental triggers like UV light or infections

summary: IBS is a common disorder of the gut that affects how the bowel works, causing belly pain along with changes in bowel habits. It does not damage the bowel, but symptoms can be uncomfortable and disruptive to daily life.
symptoms: symptoms eased by passing a bowel movement

summary: Fibromyalgia is a long-term condition that causes widespread pain, fatigue, and tenderness throughout the body. It is thought to involve how the brain and nerves process pain signals, making the body more sensitive to discomfort.
causes: altered pain processing in the nervous system

summary: Crohn's disease is a type of inflammatory bowel disease where the immune system causes inflammation in the digestive tract. It can affect any part of the gut from mouth to anus and tends to flare and settle over time.

OCD is a mental health condition involving unwanted, repeated thoughts (obsessions) and behaviours done to relieve the anxiety they cause (compulsions). These cycles can take up a lot of time and interfere with daily life.
symptoms: intense need to check things repeatedly
causes: stressful life events as a trigger

summary: POTS is a condition that affects blood flow and heart rate when standing up, causing the heart to race and the person to feel dizzy or faint. It happens because the body struggles to regulate blood pressure with changes in position.
causes: dysfunction of the autonomic nervous system

summary: Insomnia is ongoing difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or getting restful sleep, even when there's a chance to do so. Over time it can affect mood, focus, and overall health.
symptoms: waking up often during the night
feeling tired after a full night's sleep

summary: Asthma is a long-term lung condition where the airways become inflamed and narrow, making it hard to breathe. Symptoms can be triggered by allergens, exercise, cold air, or infections and range from mild to life-threatening.

Diabetes is a condition where blood sugar levels become too high because the body can't make or properly use insulin. Type 1 is an autoimmune condition, while type 2 is linked to insulin resistance and is more common.
Alzheimer's is a progressive brain disease that gradually destroys memory and thinking skills. It is the most common cause of dementia and usually affects older adults, worsening slowly over years.
symptoms: memory loss that disrupts daily life
getting confused about time or place
difficulty with planning and problem solving
causes: buildup of amyloid and tau proteins in the brain

summary: Cystic fibrosis is an inherited condition that causes thick, sticky mucus to build up in the lungs and digestive system. This leads to breathing problems and difficulty absorbing nutrients, and requires lifelong management.
symptoms: poor weight gain despite good appetite
causes: inherited mutations in the CFTR gene
passed down when both parents are carriers

summary: Endometriosis is a condition where tissue similar to the lining of the uterus grows outside it, causing pain and sometimes fertility problems. The misplaced tissue responds to hormonal cycles, leading to inflammation and scarring.
causes: tissue spreading backward through the fallopian tubes

summary: Anemia means the blood doesn't have enough healthy red blood cells to carry oxygen around the body. It often leaves people feeling tired and weak, and it has many possible causes ranging from iron deficiency to chronic illness.
causes: inherited conditions affecting red blood cells

summary: Celiac disease is an autoimmune condition where eating gluten damages the lining of the small intestine. This makes it hard to absorb nutrients and can cause a wide range of digestive and whole-body symptoms.

Tourette's syndrome is a neurological condition that causes sudden, repeated movements or sounds called tics that a person can't easily control. Tics usually start in childhood and often become milder in adulthood.
symptoms: repeated blinking, shrugging, or jerking movements
tics that worsen with stress or excitement
a building urge before a tic
causes: differences in brain regions controlling movement

summary: Psoriasis is a long-term autoimmune skin condition that speeds up the growth of skin cells, leading to thick, scaly patches. It can flare and settle, and sometimes affects the joints as well.
symptoms: raised red patches with silvery scales
dry, cracked skin that may bleed
stiff, swollen joints in some people
causes: triggers like stress, infection, or skin injury
treatments: topical corticosteroids and vitamin D creams

summary: Dyslexia is a common learning difference that mainly affects reading, spelling, and writing, despite normal intelligence. It involves how the brain processes language and is a lifelong condition that can be managed with the right support.
causes: differences in how the brain processes language
differences in brain structure and function

summary: Scoliosis is a sideways curve of the spine that often develops during the growth spurt before puberty. Many cases are mild, but more severe curves can affect posture, comfort, and in rare cases breathing.

Hemophilia is an inherited bleeding disorder where the blood doesn't clot properly because it lacks certain clotting factors. People with it bleed for longer than usual, sometimes into joints and muscles.
symptoms: bleeding into joints causing swelling and pain
prolonged bleeding after injury or surgery

summary: Schizophrenia is a serious mental health condition that affects how a person thinks, feels, and perceives reality. It can involve hallucinations, delusions, and disorganized thinking, and is usually managed long-term with treatment and support.
symptoms: hearing voices or seeing things others don't
causes: stress or substance use as triggers

summary: Lyme disease is an infection spread through the bite of an infected blacklegged tick. Caught early it's usually treatable with antibiotics, but if missed it can cause longer-lasting joint, nerve, and heart problems.

Tuberculosis (TB) is a bacterial infection that mainly affects the lungs but can spread to other parts of the body. It spreads through the air and can stay dormant for years before becoming active and contagious.
symptoms: a cough lasting more than three weeks
causes: higher risk with weakened immune systems
treatments: completing the full treatment to prevent resistance

summary: Sarcoidosis is an inflammatory condition where tiny clusters of immune cells called granulomas form in organs, most often the lungs. Its cause isn't fully understood, and it can range from mild to serious depending on which organs are involved.
symptoms: red or tender bumps on the skin

summary: Ehlers-Danlos syndromes are a group of inherited conditions that affect connective tissue, which supports the skin, joints, and blood vessels. They commonly cause very flexible joints and stretchy, fragile skin.

Graves' disease is an autoimmune condition that causes the thyroid gland to become overactive, releasing too much thyroid hormone. This speeds up the body's processes and can affect the eyes and skin.

Multiple sclerosis is a condition where the immune system attacks the protective covering around nerves, disrupting signals between the brain and body. Symptoms vary widely and can come and go or gradually worsen over time.
causes: autoimmune attack on the nerve coating (myelin)
low vitamin D and other environmental factors

summary: Huntington's disease is an inherited condition that causes the gradual breakdown of nerve cells in the brain. It affects movement, thinking, and mood, and usually appears in mid-adulthood, worsening over time.
causes: inherited mutation in the HTT gene
passed down from an affected parent

summary: Vasculitis is a group of conditions where the blood vessels become inflamed, which can restrict blood flow and damage organs. It varies widely depending on which vessels are affected and can range from mild to serious.
ITP is a condition where the immune system mistakenly destroys platelets, the blood cells that help with clotting. With fewer platelets, people bruise and bleed more easily than normal.
symptoms: tiny red or purple spots on the skin
causes: sometimes linked to other autoimmune conditions
treatments: removing the spleen in some cases

summary: Bell's palsy is a sudden weakness or drooping on one side of the face, caused by temporary problems with the facial nerve. It usually appears quickly and most people recover within weeks to months.
symptoms: sudden drooping on one side of the face
pain around the jaw or ear

summary: Eczema is a common condition that makes skin red, dry, and itchy. It often flares and settles, can run in families, and is linked to allergies and a sensitive skin barrier.
causes: triggers like soaps, allergens, or stress

summary: Postpartum depression is a serious form of depression that can develop after having a baby. It's more intense and longer-lasting than the common 'baby blues' and is treatable with the right support.
causes: lack of support or added stress
treatments: newer medications developed for postpartum depression

summary: Leprosy, also called Hansen's disease, is a slow-developing bacterial infection that affects the skin and nerves. It is curable with antibiotics, and early treatment prevents lasting nerve damage and disability.
symptoms: loss of sensation in hands and feet

summary: Anxiety is a mental health condition involving excessive worry or fear that's hard to control and interferes with daily life. It's very common and treatable, and can show up with both emotional and physical symptoms.

Alopecia is hair loss that can affect the scalp or the whole body. One common form, alopecia areata, is an autoimmune condition where the immune system attacks hair follicles, causing patchy hair loss.
symptoms: complete scalp hair loss in some cases
causes: autoimmune attack on hair follicles (alopecia areata)

summary: Rabies is a serious viral infection spread through the bite or saliva of an infected animal. It attacks the nervous system and is almost always fatal once symptoms appear, but it can be prevented with prompt treatment after exposure.
symptoms: tingling or pain at the bite site
causes: common carriers include bats, raccoons, and dogs
treatments: treatment must begin before symptoms appear
no effective treatment once symptoms start

summary: Bronchitis is inflammation of the airways that carry air to the lungs, causing coughing and mucus. Acute bronchitis often follows a cold and clears up on its own, while chronic bronchitis is a long-term condition usually linked to smoking.
treatments: treating chronic cases as part of COPD

summary: Colour blindness is a vision difference that makes it hard to tell certain colours apart, most often reds and greens. It's usually inherited, present from birth, and doesn't get worse over time.
symptoms: trouble telling red and green apart
causes: inherited gene differences affecting eye cells
rarely caused by eye disease or aging

summary: Ataxia is a loss of muscle control and coordination, affecting movements like walking, speaking, and grasping objects. It's a symptom of problems in the part of the brain that controls coordination, and has many possible causes.
Urinary tract infections happen when bacteria infect part of the urinary system, most often the bladder. They're very common, especially in women, and are usually treated easily with antibiotics.
symptoms: needing to pee often and urgently
feeling unwell or feverish if it spreads
causes: more common in women due to anatomy
treatments: prompt treatment to prevent kidney infection

summary: Polycystic kidney disease (PKD) is an inherited condition where fluid-filled cysts grow in the kidneys, gradually enlarging them and reducing their function. Over time it can lead to high blood pressure and kidney failure. (Note: the original list used the abbreviation 'PDK' — this entry assumes PKD was intended.)
symptoms: a feeling of fullness in the belly
causes: autosomal recessive form (rarer, appears in childhood)
treatments: dialysis or transplant for kidney failure

summary: Turner's syndrome is a genetic condition affecting females, where one of the X chromosomes is missing or incomplete. It can affect growth, development, and fertility, and is usually managed with hormone treatments and regular monitoring.

Hydrocephalus is a buildup of fluid in the cavities deep within the brain. The extra fluid raises pressure on the brain and can cause symptoms that vary by age, often needing surgery to drain the fluid.
symptoms: in babies, a rapidly growing head
causes: overproduction or poor absorption of fluid
present at birth or developing later
treatments: surgically placed shunt to drain fluid

summary: Influenza, or the flu, is a contagious respiratory infection caused by influenza viruses. It tends to come on suddenly and can range from mild to severe, with yearly vaccines helping to reduce risk.
causes: spread through coughs, sneezes, and contact

summary: Epilepsy is a neurological condition where bursts of abnormal electrical activity in the brain cause recurring seizures. Seizures vary widely, and many people manage the condition well with medication.
Hypothyroidism is when the thyroid gland doesn't make enough thyroid hormone, slowing down the body's processes. It develops gradually and is usually managed easily with daily hormone replacement.
treatments: regular blood tests to adjust dose

summary: Gallstones are hardened deposits that form in the gallbladder, a small organ that stores digestive fluid. Many people have no symptoms, but a stone that blocks a duct can cause sudden, severe pain and may need surgery.
symptoms: sudden pain in the upper right belly
yellowing of skin if a duct is blocked
causes: risk factors like obesity and rapid weight loss
treatments: medications to dissolve stones in some cases

summary: Gout is a form of arthritis caused by a buildup of uric acid crystals in the joints, leading to sudden, intense pain. It often strikes the big toe first and comes in painful flare-ups.
symptoms: sudden severe joint pain, often in the big toe
flares that ease over days to weeks
causes: diet high in red meat, seafood, or alcohol

summary: Menopause is the natural stage when periods stop and the ovaries make less estrogen, usually around age 50. The transition can bring a range of symptoms as the body adjusts to changing hormone levels.
causes: can be triggered by surgery or cancer treatment
treatments: support for bone and heart health

summary: Sickle cell disease is an inherited blood disorder where red blood cells become rigid and crescent-shaped. These cells can block blood flow, causing pain and other complications, and the condition requires lifelong care.
causes: passed down when both parents carry the gene
treatments: newer gene therapies and stem cell transplant

summary: COPD is a long-term lung disease that makes breathing difficult due to damaged and narrowed airways. It's usually caused by smoking and gets worse over time, though treatment can slow it and ease symptoms.

ALS is a progressive disease that attacks the nerve cells controlling voluntary muscles. Over time it leads to muscle weakness and loss of movement, while thinking is often unaffected. It currently has no cure.
symptoms: muscle weakness, often starting in a limb

summary: Malaria is a serious disease caused by parasites spread through the bite of infected mosquitoes. It causes flu-like illness and can be life-threatening, but it's preventable and treatable with the right medication.

Migraines are a neurological condition causing intense, often throbbing headaches, usually on one side of the head. They can come with nausea and sensitivity to light and sound, and may be preceded by warning signs called auras.
causes: changes in brain activity and chemicals
triggers like stress, foods, or hormones

summary: Marfan syndrome is an inherited condition affecting the body's connective tissue, which supports the heart, blood vessels, bones, and eyes. People are often tall and slender, and the main health concern is its effect on the heart and aorta.
symptoms: chest that sinks in or sticks out
causes: inherited mutation in the FBN1 gene
can occur from a new mutation
treatments: surgery to repair the aorta if needed

summary: Sleep apnea is a condition where breathing repeatedly stops and starts during sleep. It disrupts rest and lowers oxygen levels, leading to daytime tiredness and, over time, increased health risks if untreated.
symptoms: pauses in breathing noticed by others

summary: Mixed connective tissue disease is an autoimmune condition that combines features of lupus, scleroderma, and other connective tissue diseases. Symptoms overlap and vary, and it's managed by treating the active problems.
symptoms: fingers turning white or blue in the cold

summary: Complex regional pain syndrome is a condition of long-lasting, severe pain that usually affects an arm or leg, often after an injury. The pain is more intense and prolonged than expected and may come with skin and temperature changes.
symptoms: changes in skin, hair, and nail growth
causes: abnormal nerve and immune response after injury

summary: Amyloidosis is a rare condition where an abnormal protein called amyloid builds up in organs and tissues, affecting how they work. It can involve the heart, kidneys, nerves, and other organs, and varies widely between people.
symptoms: swelling in the legs or belly
numbness or tingling in hands and feet
an enlarged tongue in some cases
treatments: stem cell transplant in some cases

summary: Porphyria is a group of rare disorders caused by problems making heme, a component of the blood. Depending on the type, it can affect the nervous system, the skin, or both, and symptoms often come in episodes called attacks.
symptoms: skin that blisters or burns in sunlight
causes: triggers like certain drugs, fasting, or sunlight
treatments: glucose or hemin infusions for some attacks

summary: Undifferentiated connective tissue disease is an autoimmune condition with signs of connective tissue disease that don't fit neatly into a specific diagnosis like lupus. It's often mild and may stay stable or, in some people, develop into a defined condition over time.
symptoms: fingers turning white or blue in the cold

summary: Stiff person syndrome is a rare neurological condition that causes muscle stiffness and painful spasms that come and go. It's thought to be autoimmune, and over time it can affect posture and movement.
symptoms: muscle stiffness in the trunk and limbs
stiffness triggered by noise or stress

summary: Cushing's syndrome happens when the body is exposed to too much of the hormone cortisol over a long time. It can result from steroid medications or from the body making too much cortisol, and it affects weight, skin, and overall health.
symptoms: weight gain around the middle and face
high blood pressure and mood changes

summary: Wilson's disease is an inherited condition where copper builds up in the body because the liver can't remove it properly. The excess copper damages the liver and brain, but treatment can manage it well, especially when started early.
causes: inherited gene mutation affecting copper removal
passed down when both parents carry the gene

summary: Functional neurological disorder involves real, often disabling neurological symptoms like weakness or seizures that aren't caused by structural damage to the nervous system. Instead, it's a problem with how the brain sends and receives signals, and it can improve with the right treatment.
causes: physical or psychological stress as triggers

summary: Multiple endocrine neoplasia (MEN) syndromes are inherited conditions that cause tumours to form in two or more hormone-producing glands. The tumours are often non-cancerous but can overproduce hormones and cause a range of problems.
causes: different types (MEN1, MEN2) caused by different genes

summary: Acromegaly is a rare hormonal condition where the body makes too much growth hormone in adulthood, usually from a non-cancerous pituitary tumour. This causes gradual enlargement of the hands, feet, and facial features.
symptoms: rings and shoes becoming too tight
causes: rarely, tumours elsewhere in the body
